newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Christian Democrat leaders meet in Brussels on EU.
newsitem.headline: Christian Democrat leaders meet in Brussels on EU.

text.p: Centrist leaders from across the European Union were to meet in Brussels later on Tuesday to discuss reform of the bloc's treaty and its enlargement into eastern Europe.

The summit of the European People's Party (EPP) was to bring together German Chancellor Helmut Kohl, Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar, Irish Prime Minister John Bruton and Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi, Luxembourg Premier Jean-Claude Juncker and Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Claude Dehaene.
A spokesman for the EPP, a grouping of mainly Christian Democrat politicians, said the long-planned meeting was to discuss the state of the EU's inter-governmental conference (IGC) and new members.
Economic and monetary union (EMU) was not on the announced agenda, but would almost certainly be raised, the spokesman said.
"I'd be a bit surprised if it didn't talk about that," the spokesman said of the meeting, which he added was in no way linked to current market talk about a possible delay to EMU.
"This is not an emergency meeting. It was decided in December," he said.
